package_info.why_malicious: Trickbot is a modular banking Trojan and botnet malware that performs credential theft, lateral movement, and ransomware deployment. The latest version introduces advanced detection evasion by injecting malicious DLLs directly into legitimate Windows processes from memory, making it harder to detect and remove.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious DLL is loaded into memory and injected into the running wermgr.exe process using code adapted from the open-source 'MemoryModule' project, without writing the DLL to disk.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware loads a malicious DLL into memory and injects it directly into the wermgr.exe process using in-memory techniques, enabling execution of malicious code within a trusted Windows process and evading disk-based detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting code into legitimate system processes from memory is a common technique used by advanced malware to evade detection and maintain persistence.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software does not inject arbitrary DLLs into unrelated system processes, especially not from memory without touching disk.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some security or debugging tools may use similar techniques for legitimate process introspection or memory analysis.
key_indicators: Targeting of wermgr.exe (Windows Error Reporting Manager)

attack_chain.action: Trickbot is delivered to the victim system and executed.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware loads its modules and prepares for further actions.

attack_chain.action: Malware loads a malicious DLL into memory and injects it into the wermgr.exe process using MemoryModule code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code runs within a trusted Windows process, evading detection.

attack_chain.action: Injected code performs credential theft, lateral movement, or further payload delivery (e.g., ransomware).
attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration, system compromise, or ransomware deployment.

behavioral_signatures: In-memory DLL injection into system processes (e.g., wermgr.exe)
Use of MemoryModule or similar reflective DLL loading techniques
Execution of code in the context of Windows Error Reporting Manager
file_indicators: Unusual activity or memory regions in wermgr.exe
Absence of corresponding DLL files on disk despite loaded modules
network_indicators: C2 communications typical of Trickbot (various IPs/domains, encrypted traffic)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for in-memory DLL injection into system processes such as wermgr.exe, especially when no corresponding DLL file exists on disk. Use EDR or memory forensics to detect reflective DLL loading (e.g., MemoryModule patterns). Alert on unexpected network activity originating from wermgr.exe or other system processes. Correlate with known Trickbot C2 infrastructure and behavioral patterns.
